edges.description: Encapsulated Klebsiella cells are phagocytosed but persist in vacuolated macrophages instead of being cleared.
K. rhinoscleromatis infection induces IL-10, and this cytokine milieu is required for atypical inflammatory monocytes to mature into Mikulicz cells.
Mikulicz-cell maturation is accompanied by a dense inflammatory plasmacytic infiltrate with Russell bodies.
Chronic granulomatous inflammation progresses to a sclerotic fibrotic stage, narrowing the upper airway and distorting the nose.
Granulomatous intranasal masses obstruct the nasal airway.
Inflamed intranasal mucosa produces rhinorrhea during upper-airway disease.
Chronic inflammatory intranasal lesions can bleed, producing epistaxis.
Fibrotic luminal stenosis mechanically narrows the upper airway.
Laryngotracheal stenosis mechanically narrows the upper airway and produces noisy obstructed breathing.
Laryngeal stenosis and scarring can impair phonation and produce dysphonia.
Pharyngeal and laryngeal extension can obstruct the upper aerodigestive tract and interfere with swallowing.
Rural poverty, crowding, poor sanitation, and malnutrition have been proposed as cofactors that favor transmission or persistence of the organism.
The infected mouse lung reproduces recruitment and IL-10-dependent maturation of atypical inflammatory monocytes into Mikulicz-like foamy macrophages.
edges.limitations: Pulmonary intranasal inoculation recapitulates Mikulicz-cell maturation in mouse lungs, not chronic human nasal disease, persistent upper-airway spread, or the later fibrotic sclerotic stage.
